A: **Options:** 1) Demo Line: electrician repairs, crowd watches. 2) Fault Families: group by symptom. **Build Fault Families.** Twelve chairs as three pods: dead, intermittent, jammed. Electrician rotates 20 minutes per pod; visitors open same-fault devices together. Example: three dead kettles arrive; first visitor learns fuse test, checks second kettle, coaches third while electrician only verifies. **Test:** next Saturday swap brands within pod. If second-time visitors fix an unseen brand unaided, skill generalized; if they freeze, they only mimicked.
B: **Options:** 1) Both play full-out. 2) Clockwork Tides: pre-agreed alternating roles. **Build Clockwork Tides.** Agree on 15-minute blocks by church clock; in each block one end is Harbor (soft drone, easy to leave) and other is Beacon (lively tunes, easy to join), then swap regardless of case coins. Crowd shuttles instead of pooling. Volume stays under cap. Example: 8:00 east Beacon, west Harbor; 8:15 flip. **Test:** compare empty-case minutes versus a both-full night. If total tips hold and neither case sits empty >10 minutes, oscillation beats competition.
C: **Options:** 1) Shuffle pile nightly. 2) Ticketed Loop with public log. **Build Ticketed Loop.** Day volunteer slips each tape into numbered sleeve, gives depositor matching ticket, logs number in binder. Night player airs sleeves in numerical order, three hours, one pass max per number, writing played numbers on door sheet. Missed or doubled numbers are debts/credits corrected tomorrow. Example: #14 plays Tuesday; owner sees #14 on door Wednesday, knows it aired. **Test:** plant two marked tapes one week. If both appear once on door log and air check, fairness and traceability beat shuffle.
D: **Options:** 1) Farewell plaque chosen by council. 2) Seasonal salvage chosen by crossers. **Build Seasonal Salvage.** Each seasonal meeting, daily crossers nominate one keepable fragment — rail, lamp, rivets — and vote where it lives in the new crossing. Modest budget funds cleaning and remounting only. Example: winter picks iron lattice; engineers cast its pattern into new parapet panels. Summer picks toll-bell ritual for opening day. **Test:** survey crossers to name what was kept and where. If most can point to it on the new bridge, co-authorship beats plaque.
